chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, who said:

I heard Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: There is no prophet in the heavens or on earth who does not ask Allāh the Exalted for permission to go to the Ziyārah of Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him). A crowd descends and a crowd ascends.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Al-Ḥusayn (Imām Al-Ḥusayn ibn 'Alī, peace be upon him)
key_terms.زِيَارَةِ: Ziyārah (visitation, specifically to the shrine of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: Do prophets visit the shrine of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) stating that every prophet from the heavens and earth seeks divine permission to visit the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), with angels and prophets descending and ascending in this act of reverence. This hadith underscores the unique spiritual station of Imam al-Husayn, positioning his martyrdom as a focal point of cosmic worship and intercession, revered even by the highest prophets. The imagery of 'fouls' descending and ascending reflects the continuous, dynamic nature of this celestial pilgrimage, emphasizing the eternal significance of Karbala in Shia theology.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ‘Ammār, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: There is no prophet in the heavens or on earth who does not ask Allāh for permission to go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.). (There is always) a crowd (of prophets) descending (to go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)) and a crowd ascending (back to the heavens).
